Yes, Christopher has worked with both MCP (Model Context Protocol) and RAG. 

It is a real project, not just a course:
- **Shared Knowledge Hub (RAG) for AI Agents (MCP):** Since July 2026, Christopher has been co-leading this team-internal project at DATEV with a colleague. It is a shared context store (using a hybrid search combining BM25 keyword search and semantic embeddings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion) that connects AI coding agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Today, it is used in 10 projects, with a rollout to about 30 projects planned.
- **Certificates:** In addition to this practical work, he also holds online course certificates from Anthropic (all issued in November 2026), including *“Claude Academy: Introduction to Model Context Protocol”* and *“Claude Academy: Model Context Protocol: Advanced topics”*.

AgentBrain is a private project by Christopher that he has been working on since October 2026. 

It is a multi-agent system built on Claude Code. It features an Obsidian vault that holds notes, and a manager agent that distributes tasks to ten specialist agents (covering areas such as video, development, research, career, and design). The system includes shared memory, skills, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. 

Key details of AgentBrain include:
- **Local Vault Search:** It uses a local vault search running in a single call (combining keywords, vectors, and link graphs). In Christopher's own testing with 187 questions, this search was 49% cheaper than his previous search while maintaining the same answer quality.
- **Model Usage:** The agents use cloud models, while only the search runs locally.
- **Context:** Claude Code is a private tool used by Christopher daily for this project; it is not used at his workplace, DATEV.
No, Claude Code is not used at DATEV. At DATEV, Christopher works with GitHub Copilot. He uses Claude Code as a private tool daily in his private project, AgentBrain.
